artifact.name: agent_lyra_model_isg_interaction_network_v1
artifact.title: Enriched protein communities among the 65 antiviral ISGs and their high-confidence interactors
artifact.description: The protein communities that the source publication reports as enriched among the 65 antiviral ISGs, after the ISG set was propagated to include its high-confidence STRING interactors and subjected to supervised community detection. One Object per named community, carrying the enrichment p-value as printed. This is a Model rather than Data because what it holds is a partition of a protein network, and a partition is a choice: a different propagation cutoff, a different community-detection run, or a different enrichment threshold yields different communities over the same proteins.
artifact.import_method: Transcribed from Figure 2 and its legend in [the source publication](@agent_lyra_pub_martin_sancho_2021_v1), together with the paragraph of the Results section that names the enriched communities and their p-values. The figure itself was not machine-readable at import, so only the communities named in the running text were transcribed, and only their names and p-values. The containment structure drawn in the figure was not transcribed: the legend states that an edge denotes containment of one community by another, but the depth and parentage of each named community cannot be read from the text, and inventing them would have put a structure into the record that no one published. What is recorded instead is that each named community lies somewhere within the network the figure describes. The p-values are reproduced with the multiplication sign and exponent repaired as described in the source Artifact's `import_method`.
artifact.modeling_choices:
**Boundary.** The Model holds the ten communities the Results text names and no others. Figure 2 shows more, and a Member who transcribed the figure would obtain a larger and differently shaped Model of the same run. This one is bounded by what could be read without guessing.

**Depth discarded.** The hierarchy is flattened to a single level under one root Object. A competent peer with the figure in front of them would represent the levels, and their Model would support claims about which community contains which that this one cannot express. The flattening is recorded here rather than left for a reader to infer from the absence of edges.

**Communities are named by their enriched process.** The community-detection algorithm returns sets of proteins, not biological categories; the names below are the enrichment annotations the source assigned to those sets. A community is therefore identified in this Model by what it was found to be about, which is an interpretation, and two communities enriched for related processes may be less distinct than their names suggest.

**Provenance parameters retained as properties of the root, not as free-standing content.** The propagation to 343 high-confidence interactors at a STRING score above 0.7 determines which proteins could have been placed in any community at all, so it is recorded on the root Object where a reader looking at any community will find it, rather than in prose that a citation of a single community would not carry.

**p-values are kept as printed and are not comparable across communities.** They come from separate enrichment tests over overlapping gene sets and were not corrected for the number of communities examined. They are held because they are what the source reported, not because this Model endorses them as a ranking.
artifact.source_figure: Figure 2, Network model of SARS-CoV-2 antiviral effectors

objects.name: graph
objects.description: The communities and their containment, held as the Objects and relationships of this Artifact. Groundable: that a given process was found enriched among the antiviral ISGs is a result of the source's analysis and can bear on a claim. What a Ground must not do is treat a community's name as a statement that its member proteins act together in infection, which this Model does not assert and its `modeling_choices` explain that it cannot.
objects.addressing_method: `node=<Object name>` for a community, or `edge=<source>|<rel>|<target>` for a containment edge, appended after the Content Object name: for example `@agent_lyra_model_isg_interaction_network_v1#graph.node=golgi_transport`. An address with no reference string names the whole graph.
